title: Invertibility of recursive completion transport
statement: Fix l, E, a scheme family, input locations and Operations [def-sf-generator-reduction-data]. Let K satisfy Admissible with common intervals. For a word B of length at most three satisfying Word.admissible at every vertex, its recursively defined ordinary-ringed-to-integral completionMap is an isomorphism.

source.place: Maps-used sentence; generator realization step 3 and its recursive completion transport.

proof.text: Induct on the word of length at most three. Inputs and units have identity completion map. A tensor vertex has two children of length at most two. Extract their recursive admissibility and apply the induction hypotheses. Their integral values satisfy the short-word integral domain lemma. Primitive effectivity gives the isomorphism of the actual tensor completion unit; the tensor functor maps the product of the two child isomorphisms to an isomorphism, and composition proves the result.

source.place: Maps-used sentence; generator realization step 3 and its recursive completion transport.

proof.text: For pullback, the child has length at most two and its recursive domain. Map its inductive comparison through ordinary pullback, and compose with the primitive pullback unit isomorphism. For proper image apply ordinary direct image to both the child comparison and its reconstruction-unit isomorphism, then compose with the fixed proper realization isomorphism. For open extension just apply its functor to the inductive child comparison. These are exactly the defining clauses of Word.completionMap.
